body: A few concrete gaps between what the spec claims and what it establishes. (1) Sample size: the project idea specifies N = 5,000 functions, while the spec's acceptance scenarios, success criteria, and power assumption all use 1,000 — the discrepancy is never reconciled. (2) The 0.15 cross-model tolerance in SC-006 is circularly justified: it cites 'pilot analyses' that cannot exist at the spec stage of a project whose core data-generation pipeline has not yet been built. The tolerance is asserted, not established. (3) The HallucinationIndex treats the CodeSearchNet reference docstring as ground truth, but docstrings in that corpus are crowd/community-written and frequently incomplete or wrong; a low entity-F1 may reflect docstring quality rather than model hallucination. The manual-validation in FR-009/FR-011 validates the metric against the same reference-based scoring logic, so it cannot detect this confound. (4) Feasibility: 4-bit quantization via Hugging Face Transformers (bitsandbytes) is not supported on CPU-only runners — the assumption that starcoderbase-1b runs 4-bit quantized CPU-only is technically unverified. (5) codegen-350M is a left-to-right code-completion model, not instruction-tuned; prompting it to produce a 'single-sentence API description' will often yield code continuations, and the FR-002 fallback (truncate to 64 tokens) will convert code fragments into 'descriptions,' contaminating the HallucinationIndex. (6) The semantic-similarity component's encoder is never named in the spec (the idea's methodology is truncated mid-sentence), yet FR-020 requires validating it — validating an unspecified component.
